reelection.rule: Rule: next even-year November for this House term. legislators-current.yaml ends the current term on 2027-01-03. The even-year November before that January 3 end is November 2026. The file has no election day, so no day of the month is shown.

vote_frequency.label: In this cached set only (the latest 40 House roll calls, not a lifetime record): 40 of 40. Yea or Aye: 35. Nay or No: 5. Not Voting: 0. Of 40 Yea or Nay votes where the Republican majority could be computed, 40 (100%) matched that majority (majority = the side most of that party's members voting Yea or Nay took; on average 210 members of that party voted Yea or Nay per roll call).

posts.text:
Today, we honor and remember the lives lost in the terrorist attacks of September 11, 2001. 25 years later, we continue to remember the sacrifices of so many of our fellow Americans. 

Please join me today in honoring their memory. https://t.co/sKHqYu5Qxd

Consideration of my FY27 Homeland Security Bill resumes shortly.

As my final @HouseAppropsGOP measure, I'm proud of what it produces for the American people because our communities and nation cannot thrive without confidence in our safety and security.

https://t.co/TJEAe3kRfe

My FY27 Homeland Security @HouseAppropsGOP bill advanced out of subcommittee this morning.

Our focus is ensuring our communities remain safe, secure, and resilient. This bill provides the resources to carry out that mission.

On to full committee next week: https://t.co/Dw3XftUR4t

Summer travel season is almost here. Don’t let an expired passport ruin your plans. ✈️🌎

I’m hosting a Passport Fair on June 13 at the Reno + Sparks Chamber of Commerce to help you get passport-ready before your next big trip. Spots are limited, so be sure to sign up today! https://t.co/5lwpWPYDOw

Dedicating your life to public safety is not an easy path to choose. National Police Week is a reminder of the incredible courage our law enforcement officers bring to work every single day, and the quiet sacrifices their families make alongside them.

To every officer in CD-2: thank you for answering the call. We stand behind you.

The White House Correspondents’ Dinner was another stark reminder of how dangerous the ongoing DHS shutdown truly is. Threats don’t pause when Congress fails to do its job.

I’m grateful the Secret Service acted swiftly to secure the scene, but the reality is they are operating with strained resources, limited support, and heightened tensions.

Their mission should be singular and uncompromised: protecting our leaders and the public. We must recognize the stakes, set aside the politics, and FULLY fund DHS.

https://t.co/7uo4gH6O2l

Today, @HouseAppropsGOP heard from DHS agency leaders about their vision for FY27 and the resources needed to carry it out.

It served as a reminder that the essential work they do every day isn’t about party lines, it’s about delivering for constituents in every congressional district, including blue ones.

When it comes to the safety and security of the American people, there’s no room for political charades. Hopefully, we’ve learned a few lessons from the last rodeo and can handle things with a little more maturity this time around.

Yesterday, Nevada experienced a 5.7-magnitude earthquake. Being prepared for sudden strikes is imperative to public safety, even if it’s just a few seconds warning.

This year, I secured funding to expand the ShakeAlert early warning system into Nevada, which has proven effective in neighboring states.

Knowing our history, this may not be an isolated event. Have a plan, be prepared, and stay safe!

https://t.co/GIFYHgudVw

Make no mistake, these shutdown charades are nothing more than an attempt by Democrats to advance their anti-deportations messaging and shield the worst first and those with final orders of removal from the policy realities that this administration ran and won on.

This is the third time the House has voted to reopen DHS, and it won’t be the charm unless the Senate finishes the job.

Great joining Phil MacDougall at the National Automobile Museum for the What Drives Reno podcast. We talked about my time in Congress and, of course, our shared love of cars.

Whether you’re a Reno local or visitor, it’s well worth a stop. Huge credit to the staff and volunteers who’ve made it such a success since 1989.
https://t.co/CqmlkHRJl3

Overwhelmed TSA agents are missing their paychecks, relying on food donations, and forced to consider more stable work.

All of this results from Senate Democrats refusing to abandon their strategy of weaponizing shutdowns and turning a blind eye to the fallout it creates. https://t.co/Lfc9H4v1ru

While the House passed the FY26 Homeland Security bill for the second time yesterday, only 4 Democrats joined us in the effort to end the shutdown.

Its fate now rests in the Senate, and I urge our colleagues in the chamber next door to vote YES. 

This shutdown does nothing but weaken our security preparedness and leave thousands of employees and servicemembers without paychecks.

https://t.co/S2UKs4IjDS
Enough is enough. Congress must take its responsibility to fully fund the agencies that keep Americans safe seriously and end the DHS shutdown today.

As our nation celebrates its 250th anniversary and prepares to host the FIFA World Cup and the 2028 Olympics, security cannot take a back seat.

The Secret Service should be focused on strengthening its preparations to ensure the safety of every attendee, but the current shutdown undercuts its ability to do that work effectively.

The Disaster Relief Fund is running dangerously low as winter storms continue to disrupt communities across the country.

At the same time, FEMA has been forced to scale back operations to stretch already strained resources.

We need the government fully operational so emergency personnel can stay ready to respond and help Americans recover when disaster strikes.

If this government shutdown continues another week, nearly 41,000 Coast Guard service members will miss their paycheck.

They’re still conducting life-saving search and rescue missions and protecting our waterways without pause.

As threats escalate and their role becomes more consequential than ever, they deserve absolute confidence in our support.

Hacking our critical infrastructure is a known weapon Iran uses against the U.S., and CISA is tasked with preventing those attacks before they happen.

A government shutdown limits the agency’s capabilities, forcing it into a reactive posture rather than strengthening its proactive defenses at the very moment threats are increasing.

The Department of Homeland Security was born following 9/11, the deadliest terrorist attack ever carried out on American soil.

TSA is the frontline defense that ensures peace of mind, safety, and secure airways for travelers. But due to the ongoing DHS shutdown, they’re showing up to work unpaid and stretched thin.

When radical regimes are chanting “Death to America,” the last thing we should be doing is using the department that defends our homeland as a political pawn.

Safety and security should be the priority, but right now it's on the back burner. 🧵

Some facts about important things:

Democrats have kept DHS shut down for 19 days.

This is shutdown number 3 in the last 100 days.

120,000 DHS employees are working without pay.

The last Democrat shutdown cost $15 BILLION per week.

Consequences and costs mount everyday.

After years of unchecked illegal immigration, our communities are facing new risks at a time of heightened global unrest. The FBI has made clear we must remain vigilant at home and abroad. 

This week, we’ll again give Democrats the opportunity to end the DHS shutdown and fully fund the agencies that protect our people in moments like this.

Day 6 of the third Democrat-orchestrated shutdown in under a year.

Schumer is more interested in governing through shutdowns than leading through solutions.

Meanwhile, the men and women who keep America safe are working without pay as the backlog of core national security work mounts by the day.

If you oppose ICE or Border Patrol, that’s your prerogative, but DHS funds far more than immigration enforcement.

Shutting it down puts core national security functions at risk and does nothing to impact interior immigration enforcement. 

The consequences fall elsewhere. https://t.co/iUjs73xa14

Proud to partner with @unevadareno to secure $34.85 million to expand ShakeAlert earthquake early warning systems to Nevada.

This investment provides the tools needed to implement a proven system that keeps Nevadans safe and communities prepared for seismic activity. https://t.co/0zmrUZAkjU
Serving the people of Nevada has been the honor of my lifetime. Please see statement below: https://t.co/QJpg4r7Pav
